At least 18 sites were damaged, with fires reported at warehouses, a supermarket, residential areas and energy facilities, including combined heat and power plants, thermal power plants and electrical substations. Emergency crews and repair teams were working at damaged sites following the overnight strikes. 

Al Jazeera's Jonah Hull reports from Kyiv.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States is ending its military mission in Iraq, with the remaining American troops leaving the country after more than two decades of military involvement. 
Around 2,500 US troops had been stationed in Iraq at any given time over the past decade, largely in advisory roles supporting and training Iraqi forces. 
The latest withdrawal marks the end of a mission that began with the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, when about 130,000 American troops entered the country and overthrew Saddam Hussein's government. 
US forces remained as sectarian violence escalated, with President George W Bush ordering a troop surge in 2007 that brought the American presence to about 170,000 troops at its peak. 
The US declared the war over and withdrew in 2011, but returned three years later under Operation Inherent Resolve to fight ISIL after the group seized large areas of Iraq. 
The initial deployment was 275 personnel and eventually grew to more than 4,000. After Iraq declared victory over ISI
title: US troops leave Iraq after more than two decades of military involvement
